message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 2026-11-14 05:10 IST to 2026-11-15 05:10 IST (2026-11-13 23:40 UTC to 2026-11-14 23:40 UTC)  
**Scope:** Products.txt and List_of_SIA_Completed.txt only. Clear product entries were combined, obvious aliases were normalized, and duplicates were removed. DLL_software_component.txt was not read or combined.

No credible newly reported vulnerability met all inclusion criteria for the monitored primary-product inventory during this exact 24-hour window.

### MongoDB ecosystem coverage

The dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, mongod, mongos, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations, major maintained libraries and services, MongoDB-owned alerts, CVE/NVD records, GitHub Security Advisories, CISA sources, and credible security research.

No MongoDB finding fell inside the scan window. The nearest related disclosures were MongoDB-owned CVEs dated November 13, including Mongoid encryption issues and a MongoDB C# Driver deserialization issue, but their publication timestamps were before the 23:40 UTC cutoff and they were excluded as stale for this run.

### Validation notes

- The PostgreSQL 18.7/17.12/16.16/15.20/14.25 security release was dated November 12 and was excluded from this 24-hour digest.
- November 14 advisory feeds contained vulnerabilities in unrelated WordPress plugins, Red Hat-specific packages, and similarly named products; these were excluded because they did not confidently match the monitored entries.
- No new CISA KEV addition or vendor advisory in the window could be tied confidently to the assigned product scope.

Sources checked included the [MongoDB security alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts), [GitHub Advisory Database for November 14](https://github.com/advisories?query=published%3A2026-11-14), [PostgreSQL security release notice](https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/postgresql-187-1712-1616-1520-1425-and-19-rc-2-released-3442/), and [CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

**Closing:** No immediate review is recommended based solely on new disclosures in this scan window. Previously reported vulnerabilities and routine patch obligations remain outside the scope of this last-24-hours digest.
